{
 "cwd": "/workspace",
 "query": "FULL WEBSITE BRIEF – Build a static retro construction wiki / editorial site in SvelteKit

Create a polished static website called “BuildLedger Wiki” — an editorial knowledge base for construction methods, materials, jobsite terminology, safety notes, and historical building techniques. It should feel like a retro technical manual / 1970s contractor archive, but with the clean confidence and spacing of Stripe’s website. Think: Stripe-style layout discipline, beautiful cards, clear hierarchy, smooth sections, elegant navigation, BUT with retro construction colors, blueprint details, typewriter labels, paper textures, old catalog vibes.

IMPORTANT: This is only a static front-end website. No backend, no login, no database, no real API, no CMS, no live data. Use mock/static/sample content directly in the project. It should be exportable as a static SvelteKit site.

TECH
- Use SvelteKit
- Static pages only
- Responsive mobile/tablet/desktop
- Component-based structure
- No server-side features required
- No external API calls
- Sample wiki entries can be hardcoded
- Include a dark mode toggle with localStorage or simple client-side state

OVERALL STYLE
- Retro construction wiki
- Inspired by old blueprint sheets, site notebooks, equipment manuals, union training pamphlets, catalog cards
- Reference Stripe for: clean layout, elegant spacing, strong hero section, refined cards, subtle gradients, nice nav, polished SaaS-like presentation
- Colors: warm cream, faded safety orange, blueprint navy, aged paper tan, concrete gray, muted hazard yellow
- Dark mode: deep navy / charcoal background, amber highlights, blueprint grid accents
- Typography: mix of clean modern sans for readability + mono/typewriter style for labels, timestamps, article codes
- Use subtle texture effects, not messy
- Add small construction details: dashed measurement lines, blueprint grid, stamped labels, warning stripes, catalog tabs

SITE STRUCTURE

1. HEADER / NAVIGATION
- Logo: BuildLedger Wiki
- Small subtitle: “Field notes for builders, planners & curious homeowners”
- Navigation links:
  - Start Here
  - Materials
  - Methods
  - Safety
  - Tools
  - Glossary
- Search-looking input can be visual only, placeholder “Search the archive…” but it does not need to actually search
- Dark mode toggle button, clearly visible
- Mobile menu can be simple responsive stacked nav or hamburger if easy

2. HERO SECTION
Headline:
“An Illustrated Wiki for the Built World”
Subheadline:
“Plain-English construction references, material explainers, jobsite terminology, and field-tested notes — organized like a vintage manual and designed for modern readers.”
CTA buttons:
- “Browse the Wiki”
- “Open Field Guide”
Include a large editorial card on the right, like Stripe hero product panel but retro:
- “Featured Entry: Balloon Framing”
- Category badge: STRUCTURE
- Small diagram placeholder made with CSS shapes or simple lines
- 3 quick facts:
  - Common in older timber homes
  - Requires careful fire blocking
  - Often found during renovations

3. QUICK INDEX STRIP
A horizontal/stacked section with archive categories:
- Foundations
- Framing
- Masonry
- Roofing
- Concrete
- Insulation
- Electrical Basics
- Site Safety
Each should be a card/tag with a small icon-style mark made from text or CSS, no need for image assets.

4. FEATURED ARTICLES SECTION
Title: “Featured Field Notes”
Create 6 article cards with mock content:
- “Reading a Foundation Plan”
- “Concrete Slump Explained”
- “Why Roof Pitch Matters”
- “Common Brick Bonds”
- “Joist vs Beam vs Rafter”
- “Moisture Barriers 101”
Each card should include:
- Category
- Short excerpt
- Estimated read time
- Retro article code like BL-042
- Small tag chips
Cards should have Stripe-like polish: hover lift, soft shadows, clean spacing, but retro colors.

5. WIKI ARTICLE PREVIEW LAYOUT
Create a section that previews what an article page looks like:
Left side:
- Table of contents panel
- “Overview”
- “When it appears”
- “Field checks”
- “Common mistakes”
- “Related terms”
Right side:
- Article mock titled “Moisture Barrier”
- Include sample paragraphs, callout box, note box, and mini definition list
- Use editorial formatting: headings, pull quote, highlighted term, small metadata row
This should look like a serious static wiki/editorial site, not a simple landing page.

6. MATERIALS LIBRARY
Create a grid/table style section called “Materials Library”
Include static entries:
- Portland Cement
- OSB Sheathing
- Copper Pipe
- Mineral Wool
- Asphalt Shingles
- Rebar
- Type X Drywall
Each item should show:
- Use case
- Durability note
- “Watch for” note
- Tag badge like MATERIAL / SAFETY / STRUCTURE
Design like a vintage index card system.

7. TIMELINE / ARCHIVE SECTION
Title: “Construction Knowledge Through the Decades”
Retro timeline with 5 static points:
- 1880s: Balloon framing spreads through timber towns
- 1920s: Concrete standards become more formalized
- 1950s: Suburban building catalogs popularize standard plans
- 1970s: Energy codes begin changing envelope design
- 2000s: Moisture management becomes a major renovation topic
Make it visually interesting with blueprint lines and stamped year labels.

8. SAFETY CALLOUT SECTION
Must be visually strong but not scary.
Title: “Safety Notes Are Part of the Wiki”
Text: “Every topic includes plain-language cautions, common jobsite risks, and reminders to consult qualified professionals for structural, electrical, plumbing, and code-critical work.”
Include 3 cards:
- “PPE reminders”
- “Code varies locally”
- “Don’t guess on structure”
This is informational only.

9. GLOSSARY PREVIEW
Create an alphabetized mini glossary with static sample terms:
- Anchor Bolt
- Batter Board
- Birdsmouth
- Dead Load
- Flashing
- Kerf
- Plumb
- R-Value
Use a clean two-column or responsive grid layout.

10. NEWSLETTER / STATIC CTA
This should be visual only, no actual submission needed.
Title: “Get the monthly field memo”
Subtext: “A static mock newsletter form for design only — no data is collected.”
Input placeholder: “you@example.com”
Button: “Preview Signup”
Make it clear it is just front-end/static.

11. FOOTER
Include:
- BuildLedger Wiki logo
- Description
- Links: About, Editorial Policy, Glossary, Safety Notice, Contact Mockup
- Small disclaimer: “Educational reference only. Always consult licensed professionals and local code requirements.”
- Copyright line for 2026

INTERACTIONS
- Dark mode toggle must work
- Hover states on cards/buttons
- Smooth scroll or anchor links are nice if easy
- Search input is decorative only unless you want simple local filtering, but not required
- No login, no account, no admin, no backend

DESIGN DETAILS
- Use Stripe-inspired premium section spacing and card rhythm
- Retro construction pattern backgrounds: blueprint grid, paper grain via CSS, dashed lines, border stamps
- Add little labels like “ARCHIVE CARD”, “FIELD NOTE”, “REV. 06/2026”
- Use strong contrast and readable text
- Make the homepage feel complete and realistic, not placeholder-heavy
- Use sample data arrays for entries/articles/materials
- Add responsive behavior for all main sections

DELIVERABLE
A complete static SvelteKit front-end website for BuildLedger Wiki with all content mocked locally. It should run without any third-party services and should not require authentication, a database, API keys, or server functionality.",

  "request_model": "meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8:novita",
  "provider": "novita",
  "pinned_on": "2026-10-09",
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "rubric_id": "rva1:mean(visual,query,asset)"
 }
}

"""Grade a Webdev task as the explorer does (verl recipes/design webdev-eval): render, shrink, judge.

No index.html in dist/ scores 0. A render that fails, or a judge that never answers, writes no reward (not scored):
neither says anything about the page."""
import base64
import io
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/tests")
os.environ["WEBDEV_GRADE_HTTP"] = "1"   # serve over loopback http so React/Vue/ES-module sites actually run
from webdev.eval_rubric import build_prompt  # noqa: E402
from webdev.shot import _build_shot_cmd, _parse_render_env, _parse_shot_b64  # noqa: E402
from webdev.verdict import parse_verdict  # noqa: E402

cfg = json.loads(Path("/tests/grade.json").read_text())
V = Path("/logs/verifier")
V.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
dist = Path(cfg["cwd"]) / "dist"


def done(reward: float | None, why: str, **extra) -> None:
    (V / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps({"reward": reward, "summary": why, **extra}, indent=1))
    print(why)
    if reward is None:
        print("not scored", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    (V / "reward.txt").write_text(f"{reward}\n")
    sys.exit(0)


files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(dist)) for p in dist.rglob("*") if p.is_file())[:200] if dist.is_dir() else []
if "index.html" not in files:
    done(0.0, "The agent delivered nothing to dist/." if not files else "dist/ has no index.html, so there is no page to open.",
         delivered=files)
res = subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", _build_shot_cmd(f"file://{dist}/index.html")], capture_output=True, text=True,
                     timeout=150)   # SHOT_TIMEOUT_S
shot = {"output": (res.stdout or "") + "\n" + (res.stderr or "")}
shot_b64, console_errors = _parse_shot_b64(shot)
render_env = _parse_render_env(shot)
if render_env.get("proxy_failed") or not shot_b64:
    print(shot["output"][-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
    done(None, "external assets were unreachable on every route" if render_env.get("proxy_failed")
         else "the screenshot produced no image")
jpg = base64.b64decode(shot_b64)
try:   # eval_mode._shrink: the judge refuses shots over 20 MP; proportional, quality 75
    from PIL import Image
    Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(jpg))
    size = im.size
    if im.width * im.height > 20e6:
        k = (20e6 / (im.width * im.height)) ** 0.5
        im = im.convert("RGB").resize((max(1, int(im.width * k)), max(1, int(im.height * k))), Image.LANCZOS)
        b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG", quality=75); jpg = b.getvalue(); size = im.size
except ImportError:
    size = None
(V / "screenshot.jpg").write_bytes(jpg)
content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpg).decode()}},
           {"type": "text", "text": build_prompt().format(query=cfg["query"][:1500])}]   # QUERY_CAP
url = os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_URL", "https://router.huggingface.co/v1").rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"
_judge_pin = cfg["judge"]
if os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_REVISION") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
    done(None, "Judge deployment revision is unbound; not scored.")
(V / "judge_config.json").write_text(json.dumps(_judge_pin, indent=1))
body = json.dumps({"model": cfg["judge"]["request_model"], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 1024,  # webdev-temp0-pin@1
                   "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
verdict, last = None, ""
for attempt in range(4):   # JUDGE_RETRIES, with eval_mode's backoff
    if attempt:
        time.sleep(min(60.0, 3.0 * (3 ** (attempt - 1))) * (0.5 + random.random()))
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, method="POST", headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('WEBDEV_JUDGE_KEY', '')}"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:   # JUDGE_TIMEOUT_S
            _judge_reply = json.loads(r.read())
            if _judge_reply.get("model_revision") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
                done(None, "Judge response revision differs from the task pin; not scored.")
            msg = _judge_reply["choices"][0]["message"]
        v = parse_verdict(msg.get("content") or msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")
        if "_failed" not in v:
            verdict = v
            break
        last = v["_failed"]
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        last = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
if not verdict:
    done(None, f"judge unavailable: {last}")
done(verdict["score"], verdict.get("reason", ""), dims=verdict["dims"], visual=verdict["visual"], screenshot_size=size,
     console_errors=console_errors[:1500] if console_errors not in ("", "[]") else "")

rationale: Use temperature zero and bind the model/provider request and artifact revision; mask absent or mismatched deployment/response revision. Version-aware judge endpoint validation is staged.
